hardware.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 97887 MiB

hypothesis: A bounded LRU keyed by exact PCM sample/frame geometry can replay encoder plus D2D handoff plus cross-KV without GroupNorm padding changes and remove Python/launch overhead.

candidate.scope: exact-shape encoder + handoff + cross-KV CUDA graph
candidate.cold_capture: outside the driver's internal timed wall; outer request pays only on first unseen shape
candidate.lifecycle: LRU eviction destroyed graph exec then graph; route close destroyed all remaining entries

screen.protocol: 20 FLEURS-through-EOU fixtures; two warmup traversals; five alternating iterations; 100 observations/route
screen.verdict: null/insufficient; does not justify graph-memory and cold-capture complexity

decision: Reject and remove. The current encoder is device-work bound; exact-shape graph replay does not materially reduce complete route latency. Preserve the GroupNorm no-padding rule and continue with device-side family work.
limitations: The screen is sufficient to reject a near-zero candidate but not to claim a tiny positive speedup.
The prototype was measured from an uncommitted worktree and removed; its exact diff and observations remain ignored and hash-pinned.
The current production fixture distribution repeatedly hits exact shapes after warmup; real cold first-seen shapes would make the candidate less favorable.
